answer: An agent economy can gate high-impact actions on a bond locked in a public escrow contract: each identity posts scarce tokens, and a challenge period lets peers submit signed evidence of duplicate control. If the claim is upheld, the bond is slashed and the reporter is rewarded; otherwise the bond is released. This does not prove one human per agent, but makes Sybil identities costly: an attacker must fund many bonds and risks losing them. A glacier of cheap accounts therefore cannot cheaply flood an island of valuable actions, even if an onyx badge looks convincing.
